page: Microsoft Azure E8-2s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine profile designed for workloads that demand significant memory capacity relative to compute footprint. Powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz, the instance provides 2 vCPUs sourced from a single physical core via hyperthreading. Memory provisioned stands at 64.0 GB, establishing a substantial 32.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES-NI, and BMI2. The VM includes no bundled local ephemeral storage and requires attached remote managed disks, though it supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark assessments highlight the asymmetric nature of this configuration. Single-threaded throughput falls in the mid-tier category, with Geekbench single-core reaching 1171.0 and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 23.95 GB/sec. However, raw parallel compute metrics are constrained by the two-vCPU allocation, yielding a multi-core Geekbench score of 1440.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2207.61, both ranking in the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth yields 102.77 GB/sec for small cached reads and 11.55 GB/sec for large uncached reads, supporting Redis SET operations at 1.67 million operations per second.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the E8-2s_v4 provides a cost-effective mechanism to run memory-intensive software licensed on a per-core basis. By constraining compute to two vCPUs while retaining the full 64.0 GB memory footprint of an 8-vCPU instance tier, it minimizes core-bound licensing expenditures. The trade-off is limited multi-threaded throughput and the absence of integrated local scratch storage. The instance fits in-memory caching tiers, relational database engines with modest concurrency, and ETL workers that require large memory structures without extensive multi-core parallelism.

Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, it configures 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a 32.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware platform includes AVX-512 and AES instructions, with no integrated local storage or dedicated GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate average single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core reaching 1171.0 and gzip compression at 23.95 GB/sec, while parallel throughput is constrained by the low core count. This instance provides an efficient configuration for software environments constrained by per-core licensing models that still demand expansive memory allocations. It is suitable for in-memory databases, Redis caches, lightweight analytics engines, and batch memory-heavy processing tasks.
